title: Linking in Speech
subtitle: Connected Speech Flow
description: Fluent English runs words together rather than pronouncing each one separately. Learning to link sounds naturally is one of the biggest steps toward sounding native.
tip: Treat the whole phrase as one long word — when a word ends in a consonant and the next starts with a vowel, slide them together without a pause.
phrases: Turn it off and put it away before you leave.
Pick it up and bring it over to the table.
What are you up to tonight after work?
I looked it up and found out it was free.
Come on in and sit down — take it easy.
She ran out of time and had to give it up.
Let me know if you figure it out on your own.
Hold on a second — I'll be right back in a minute.
